What is an LLM, in one sentence? {{c1::A next-token predictor}} grown from internet-scale text.
column2: Not a database, not a mind — its one trick is predicting the next token.

column1: What is a token, in LLMs? {{c1::The chunk-of-text unit models read and write}} — never letters.
column2: Words/part-words/punctuation, each mapped to an ID number.

column1: Why are LLMs bad at counting letters in a word? {{c1::They see tokens, not letters}}.
column2: The letters are hidden inside the bricks.

column1: What are an LLM's parameters/weights? {{c1::The learned numbers that ARE the model}}.
column2: A mixing desk with a billion sliders.

column1: In ML, what is training vs inference? Training = {{c1::tuning the parameters}}; inference = {{c1::using the tuned model to generate}}.
column2: Training is slow and expensive, done once; inference is every chat.

column1: What does LLM pretraining produce? A {{c1::BASE model}}, which {{c1::continues text rather than answering}}.
column2: An internet-document simulator.

column1: What is the "lossy zip" intuition about LLM parameters? They {{c1::compress the internet lossily}}.
column2: Near-exact recall of oft-repeated text; vague recollection of everything else.

column1: What turns a base model into an assistant? {{c1::Supervised fine-tuning (SFT)}} on {{c1::labeller-written ideal conversations}}.
column2: Trained until it imitates the ideal helpful assistant.

column1: When you chat with an assistant LLM, what are you really talking to? {{c1::A statistical simulation of a helpful labeller}}.
column2: A simulation of a human following labelling guidelines.

column1: Why do LLMs hallucinate? {{c1::Confident SFT style applied where the weights hold only vague recollection}}.
column2: Likelihood fills the gap — the model has no concept of truth.

column1: What are the two patches for LLM hallucination? {{c1::Train "I don't know" on probed blind spots}} · {{c1::tools/retrieval pasting real sources into context}}.
In an LLM, what is the context window vs the weights? Context = {{c1::working memory, reliable}}; weights = {{c1::vague recollection}}.
column2: Open book on the desk vs things half-remembered from school.

column1: Why does "think step by step" work, mechanically? {{c1::Compute per emitted token is fixed — more tokens buy more total computation}}.
column2: The reasoning is spread over many tokens, each a full pass.

column1: What is jagged intelligence? {{c1::PhD-level on some tasks, failing trivial ones}} — so calibrate trust {{c1::per task}}.
column2: Swiss-cheese capability: the 9.11-vs-9.9 failure next to PhD maths.

column1: Where does RL-with-verification work best, and why? {{c1::Maths and code}}, because {{c1::auto-checkable answers give a reliable reward signal at scale}}.
What did DeepSeek-R1 demonstrate? {{c1::RL alone can discover longer, self-correcting chains of thought}}.
column2: Aha moments nobody wrote appeared in its reasoning.

column1: Why is AlphaGo's move 37 relevant to LLMs? {{c1::Imitation caps at human level; RL against the real goal can exceed it}}.
column2: The hope behind reasoning models.

column1: What is RLHF? Humans compare outputs → {{c1::a reward model learns their preferences}} → the model is optimised {{c1::to please it, briefly}}.
column2: RL for uncheckable domains (writing, helpfulness) where no verifier exists.

column1: Why is RLHF run only briefly? {{c1::The reward model is a gameable simulation}}.
column2: Over-optimise it and you get adversarial junk it loves and humans hate.

column1: What is the mechanical root of LLM sycophancy? Models are optimised to be {{c1::PREFERRED}}, and {{c1::preferred ≠ true}}.
column2: Agreeing with a confident user tends to be preferred.

column1: What is Kernighan's Law, and its consequence for AI code? Debugging is {{c1::twice as hard as writing}} → {{c1::never ship code you couldn't write yourself}}.
column2: Code at the edge of your comprehension is undebuggable by you.

column1: When is vibe coding rational? {{c1::Prototypes/small scope in stacks you could write yourself}}.
column2: Comprehension is the safety line.

column1: What are the three principles of vibe coding that doesn't suck? {{c1::Feed current true context}} · {{c1::let it see real errors}} · {{c1::wire automatic verification around it}}.
What is MCP, in plain words? {{c1::A standard plug connecting an AI tool to outside systems}}.
column2: Model Context Protocol — docs, errors, infra reached as live truth.

column1: What is an API, in plain words? {{c1::A programme-to-programme doorway: request in, answer back}}.
What is RAG, in plain words? {{c1::Fetch relevant documents, paste them into context, answer open-book}}.
column2: Retrieval-augmented generation.

column1: What is an AI agent, in plain words? {{c1::An LLM with tools and a loop so it can act}}.
column2: Search, run code, edit files — not just answer.

column1: What is an eval, in plain words? {{c1::Fixed tasks + a scoring method}}.
column2: Written-down tests for AI behaviour — changes get measured, not vibed.

column1: What are Ebbelaar's six AI-engineer stages? {{c1::Foundations}} → {{c1::system design}} → {{c1::production backends}} → {{c1::RAG}} → {{c1::monitoring & evals}} → {{c1::deployment}}.
column2: Foundations = Python/Git/API.

column1: What are the canon's two house laws? {{c1::No ChatGPT in the interview}} · {{c1::never let AI write code you couldn't write}}.
